Shelta is a cant or secret language used by Irish Travelers, also known as Pavees or Gypsies. It is a mix of Irish, English, and borrowed words, with a unique phonetic system. For example, the word for 'tree, bush' is 'skraꭕo', which includes the consonant /ꭕ/, a hissing sound held in the back of the throat. Some Shelta words have been borrowed by mainstream English speakers, such as the word "bloke" meaning 'a man'. There is no standard orthography for Shelta, and it can be written following an Irish-type orthography or an English-type orthography. In 1979, the mid-year changes for the US model of the Toyota Celica Supra were mostly cosmetic. The interior received a redesigned center console and a digital quartz clock. On the exterior, there were redesigned side view mirrors and 14x51⁄2 inch aluminium wheels became standard. Body molded mudflaps were also available and were painted body color on cars finished in copper metallic and white, while they were left black on all other colors. The word "Celica" was painted in white lettering on the rear of the mudflaps. Additionally, optional leather-trimmed seating and automatic climate-control were available.

For the 1981 model year, the Supra received an upgrade in displacement with the 2.8-litre 5M-E engine, which was still a 12-valve SOHC engine but had a power output of 116 hp (87 kW).
